To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
androgen regulation of coregulator gene expression is a common mechanism of AR action in PCa and that androgen‐regulated coregulator gene transcription may be a novel therapeutic target in PCa.
the expression of many AR‐coregulators are differentially regulated in PCa cells, compared to normal prostate epithelial cells, and that these changes are important for PCa cell survival.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of androgen‐responsive genes in prostate cells and how their expression is regulated.
the mechanisms underlying the androgen regulation of steroid receptor coregulator genes.
the role of steroid hormone receptors and their associated coregulators in normal and malignant prostate cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
androgen regulates the expression of coregulators in PCa cells, but the mechanisms by which androgens regulate these genes are not well defined and may be cell‐specific.
the expression of coregulators in LNCaP cells is differentially regulated by androgen.

the expression of the majority of the steroid receptor coregulator genes in PCa cells is not regulated by androgen and that androgen regulation is restricted to a subset of coregulators that is not consistent with all PCa cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
AR activity in LNCaP cells is regulated in part by the androgen regulation of coregulator gene expression.
the majority of coregulator genes are not regulated by androgen in LNCaP cells.
the expression of a subset of coregulators is under androgen regulation and that this is not a feature of normal prostate epithelial cells (PZ‐HPV‐7 cells).
The main takeaway from our work is that
androgen‐dependent coregulator expression is not limited to the AR‐associated corepressors, NCoR and SMRT, as previously reported.
